answer.evidence: Seen from behind, the main body (rows 8-24) is a single flat-colored back panel, L=101 in every scanned column. Rows 6-7 at the top are a light 2-row rim (L 199 then 176) with no eave shadow below. This is the top edge of the backrest, not a top surface. The armrests have small light caps at rows 11-13, but they are only 2-3 rows tall and have no front-edge line. The seat cannot be seen at all, because the backrest hides it. The two brown legs at rows 25-26 confirm a back view. The width profile (10, 12, 14, 16) just follows the chair outline and shows no ellipse. The chair has no visible seat surface, so it matches the 'seat: band 2' and 'front elevation' wrong references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate armchair has only 8 distinct colours against 11-40 for the references. Its 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 33%, while the references with similar structure (bench, hedge, lamp) are at 0% and the richest stall is at 13%. The back panel and body read as large flat areas of one muted tone, with a single highlight band and a dark edge. The outline does lean brown/maroon (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so it is a tinted material tone and not a sticker black. But the shading is shallow at about 3 steps against 5-6 on the references, and there is no grain, stitching, wood-leg detail or fabric texture. The median of 6 colours per tile is below the hedge (10), stall (17) and well (20). Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter.
